title: Wake up, sleepers (3:4)
hook: the shofar says: wake from your sleep, search your deeds
tomorrow: what gets in the way when you really want to change?

segments.voice: Yesterday: one deed tips the world. See the scale as level, and your next act decides. Today, from the same halakhah, the sound that's meant to remind you.
screen: `ONE DEED TIPS THE WORLD.` → `THE SOUND THAT REMINDS YOU.`

segments.voice: Snooze, once. Snooze, twice. The alarm keeps getting softer in your head, until the day is half gone before you're really in it. On Rosh Hashanah the alarm is a ram's horn, the shofar, and it doesn't come with a snooze button. So what is the shofar actually trying to say? Here the tradition holds two answers at once, and they pull in different directions.
screen: `SNOOZE, ONCE. SNOOZE, TWICE.` → `A RAM'S HORN.` → `TWO ANSWERS AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: The first answer: it isn't trying to say anything. Blowing the shofar is a decree, gezeirat hakatuv, a command of scripture. The Talmud asks, plainly, why do we blow? And answers: because the Merciful One said, blow. Here's that view at its best. If the shofar is only a message, then anyone who gets the message can skip the horn. A decree keeps the act from shrinking into a lesson you already know. You show up and do it, whether or not it moves you. The second answer is Maimonides', in the very same sentence. Although it's a decree, he writes, there's a hint in it, as if it were saying: wake up, sleepers, from your sleep. Slumberers, rise from your slumber. Search your deeds, return, and remember your Creator. You who forget the truth in the small business of the day and spend the whole year on what can't help or save you: look to your souls. That view at its best: a command you never listen to can become one more thing done half-asleep. The hint is how the act gets inside you. Maimonides doesn't choose between them. He says decree, and then he says hint, and he leaves both standing. One person can blow because they're commanded, and hear an alarm clock anyway.
screen: `A DECREE: BLOW, BECAUSE IT WAS SAID.` · `KEEPS IT FROM SHRINKING.` · `THE HINT: WAKE UP, SEARCH.` · `DECREE AND HINT, BOTH STANDING.` · then, large: `WAKE UP, SLEEPERS.`

segments.voice: Sit up tall, feet flat, shoulders back, the way a body sits when it's suddenly wide awake. Name one thing you do half-asleep, a scroll, a reply, a routine on autopilot. Keep the tall posture and look at that habit plainly until the bell.
screen: `SIT UP TALL.` · `ONE HABIT ON AUTOPILOT.` · `LOOK AT IT.`

segments.voice: Wake up: the hint Maimonides hears in the shofar. Rise from your slumber, search your deeds, return, even though the blowing itself is a decree.
Your line: wake up, sleepers. Commanded, and still an alarm clock. Day fifteen fifty, awake.

screen: `DAY 1550 COUNTS.` → `MAIMONIDES, THE LAWS OF RETURN · 13 OF 30.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT GETS IN THE WAY WHEN YOU REALLY WANT TO CHANGE?`

howItsDone: The shofar is blown in synagogue on Rosh Hashanah, and in some communities each weekday morning in the month before it, the month of Elul.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks why your family lights candles on Friday night if nobody can fully explain why. which reply holds both of today's views?
